deities: Lord Vishnu - Anantasayi (Anantasai) Vishnu (upper shrine) and Kurma Janardana (lower shrine)

history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the temple is in North Guwahati (Amingaon side), Kamrup district - NOT in Dispur, so the CSV town is wrong. The Aswakranta Devalaya stands on the hillock Ashrakut on the banks of the Brahmaputra and comprises two Vishnu shrines - the lower Kurma Janardana temple and the hilltop Aswaklanta/Anantasayi Vishnu temple - plus two rock-cut caves facing the river, all recorded as an archaeological site by the Directorate of Archaeology, Assam. The 1720 Ahom structures were built over earlier stone temple foundations; the hilltop Anantasayi Vishnu image is an 11th-century sculpture (fine art specimen), with Dasavatara and Astadikpala carvings on the walls. It was damaged in the great earthquake of 1897 and repaired in 1901 under the patronage of Lord Curzon. Legend: Lord Krishna's horse grew tired ('aswa' = horse, 'klanta' = tired) here while he went to slay Narakasura; another legend derives the name from 'Abhikranta' (Arjuna detained by conspiracy). A former sacrificial kunda nearby was eroded by the river.

name: Aswaklanta Temple
town_description: North Guwahati, on the north bank of the Brahmaputra opposite Guwahati, was the old capital region of the historic Kamrup kingdom. Today it is a quieter riverside area linked to the city by the Saraighat bridge and ferry ghats, dotted with ancient temples and archaeological sites.

travel.airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport - about 30 km (verify).
travel.railway: Amingaon station nearby (verify); Guwahati Junction about 12 km via the Saraighat bridge.
travel.road: Reached by road across the Saraighat bridge (address: Amingaon, Doul Govinda Rd, North Guwahati 781031) and by regular ferry services across the Brahmaputra from the south bank.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Janmashtami and Ashokastami draw large crowds. The riverside sunset is a highlight.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Widely reported as 7:00 AM-5:00 PM (verify). Remove footwear; carry water for the hilltop climb.
